conceptName: When a threshold aborts a run

items.stem: What does the garbage-collection / orphan percentage abort threshold protect against?

options.text: Deleting or orphaning too much of the destination because of a bad source feed
A full disk on the StarBridge server

items.explanation: The percentage thresholds halt a run that would delete/orphan more than the allowed share of the destination — the classic symptom of a broken feed returning too few rows.

misconceptions.b: It's about how much would be removed, not runtime.

items.stem: A run aborts with a garbage-collection percentage error. What's the first thing to check?

options.text: How many source rows the feed loaded (a suspiciously low count = a broken feed)

items.explanation: Check the source row count first ('Loading source system entities ... N loaded'); a broken feed returning too few rows is the usual trigger.

misconceptions.a: Raising the threshold first can turn a caught problem into data loss.

items.stem: When is it appropriate to raise an abort threshold so the run completes?

options.text: Whenever an abort is slowing you down
Only once you've confirmed the large change is legitimate and expected (e.g. a real bulk removal)
Any time the source feed looks fine at a glance

items.explanation: Raise it deliberately only when the big change is genuinely expected; otherwise the abort is correctly protecting the destination.

misconceptions.a: Forcing the run through to save time is exactly how a bad feed wipes the destination.

items.stem: An overnight run aborts: 'garbage-collection percentage exceeded.' The console shows the Staff feed loaded 120 entities; it normally loads ~5,000. What happened, and what do you do?
rubric: The source feed is broken/incomplete (120 vs ~5,000) — likely an outage, bad filter, or credential issue
The engine saw ~4,880 records as 'disappeared' and was about to garbage-collect them; the threshold aborted to protect the destination
Fix the source/feed and re-run; do NOT raise the threshold to force it through
items.sampleAnswer: The Staff feed only returned 120 of ~5,000, so it's broken (source outage, a bad query/filter, or a credential problem). The engine would have treated the ~4,880 missing records as deletions, and the GC threshold aborted to stop that — it did its job. I fix the source feed and re-run; I do not raise the threshold to push it through.
items.source: Documentation/Synnduit Deletion limit threshold setting demo.docx

items.stem: Which threshold is about 'too many errors' rather than 'too much deletion'?
items.explanation: Segment/Run abort thresholds count exceptions; the percentage thresholds bound how much of the destination can be deleted/orphaned.

misconceptions.b: The GC percentage threshold bounds deletion, not error count.
